notes: Steer from your Lock Screen. A running spoof can now be moved without opening Mirage: the Live Activity carries turn left, go/hold, turn right, a pace button and stop, on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. Two buttons rotate your heading 45° at a time and one starts or holds you, so you can walk a street grid without ever bringing the app up. A draggable floating joystick isn't possible on iOS — Picture-in-Picture is built for video and its window consumes touches before your content sees them — so this is the same idea as buttons you can actually press. Your places follow you: saved spots back up to your account and merge in on your other devices, so favourites set on your iPhone are there on your iPad, and renames and deletions travel too. A first run that shows you the app: onboarding replaces its feature list with a demo that plays itself — a tap lands on the map, a pin drops, the place card rises, Teleport is pressed, and the spoof goes live, narrated beat by beat. A held spoof also drifts a metre or two like real GPS instead of freezing on an exact point, since a perfectly still coordinate is one of the cheapest tells that a location is fake (this does not clear iOS's simulated-location flag; apps that read it still refuse). Fixed: the WiFi certificate installer no longer spins forever when the local profile server can't get on the network — it fails fast and points you at “Save profile to Files” — and Settings no longer claims you're spoofing when you aren't, which happened on a fresh launch from a leftover coordinate.
